messages:
PagerBot: 🚨 ALERT: p99 latency above SLO for /v1/generate (model: rwx-13b) in prod-us-east. p95 also drifting. triggered at 2026-03-14T12:34:16Z. paging on-call team
Maya (SRE): seeing it, joining. initial blast looks like tail latency, not queueing. clients report streaming stalls around the same time.
Elise (Support): we got 3 customer reports saying partial stream then socket reset. customers: analytics-prod and chat-widget. informing CS.
Simon (Eng-Platform): dashboard link: https://dashboard.redwood/prod/latency?svc=serve-main - p99 spiked to ~6.8s (baseline 1.2s). p95 at ~1.6s.
Jun (ServRuntime): checking infra metrics — GPU utilization normal. autoscaler not scaling up. no obvious OOMs. pulling logs from a few hosts.
Maya (SRE): I'll run a quick tail on the streaming proxy logs for errors and timeouts. run: `kubectl logs -f svc/stream-proxy -n prod --since=10m | grep -i timeout`
Maya (SRE): grep shows a flood of `connection reset by peer` and repeated `send buffer full` on 12:34:xx across 4 pods.
Jun (ServRuntime): pulling model server traces. KV cache hit rate dropped to 12% from 85% at spike start — suspicious. maybe cache invalidation storm.
Simon (Eng-Platform): Any recent rollout? I see a canary for rwx-13b-quant rolled out 12:27 but marked healthy. change history: `feature/stream-optimizations` merged earlier today.
Oncall-Shadow: handoff ack. I'm here to help, focusing on mitigation steps.
Maya (SRE): quick mitigation: route traffic away from rwx-13b-quant variant to rwx-13b-fp16 (slower tokens cost-wise but should avoid cache mismatch). Simon, can you flip routing?
Simon (Eng-Platform): starting rollout: updating routing policy to prefer variant=fp16 for prod routes. command: `redwood route update --svc serve-main --policy fallback:fp16 --weight 100`
Simon (Eng-Platform): done. routing change propagated to edge (ttl ~15s).
Elise (Support): telling affected customers we've routed traffic to fallback variant; may see slight perf/cost change.
Maya (SRE): monitoring p99 after switch...
(30s pass)
Maya (SRE): p99 dropped to ~1.4s, p95 back to baseline. streaming stalls reports reduced.
Jun (ServRuntime): KV cache metrics: hit rate recovering to ~78% now. looks like an invalidation flood caused increased compute and stalls. need root cause.
Maya (SRE): capturing cluster state, saving logs and traces for postmortem. commands: 
```
flux export traces --from 2026-03-14T12:20:00Z --to 2026-03-14T12:40:00Z -o /tmp/trace-spike.tar.gz
kubectl get pods -o wide > /tmp/pods-before-after.txt
```
Simon (Eng-Platform): I rolled back the canary for `feature/stream-optimizations` in case it's related. rollback id: canary-2026-03-14-1227.
Jun (ServRuntime): I'll look into model cache invalidation logic — suspect race when prefix caching updated during config push. adding extra instrumentation.
Elise (Support): CS updated customers with mitigation notes, ETA for follow-up 2 hours.
Maya (SRE): Incident bot: paging closed. we're in mitigation. creating incident ticket INC-2026-0314-01 and assigning to eng-runtime for RCA.
Oncall-Shadow: taking post-incident checklist: (1) preserve logs (2) collect evals to ensure no quality regressions after variant switch (3) cross-team RCA meeting 16:00 UTC.
Jun (ServRuntime): creating small repro harness to simulate prefix invalidation at scale. will share findings in RCA.
Simon (Eng-Platform): note: autoscaler alert thresholds too conservative for cache-miss storms; adding a temporary alert rule: trigger if p95>2s for 3m AND cache_hit_rate<40%.
Maya (SRE): good. final check: customers' streams restored? Elise?
Elise (Support): two customers confirmed streams normal, no data loss observed. one customer requested logs, CS attached sanitized traces.
Maya (SRE): closing live triage. leaving thread open for RCA updates. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
